title: cross-sdk cursor-adapter and token-swap reauth for streaming ergonomics
author: Maya Torres
description:
Summary:
Introduce a lightweight cross-language cursor adapter for streaming responses and a compact 'token-swap' reauthentication flow (soft backoff + immediate-swap fast-path) to make long-lived streams robust across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs. This PR focuses on ergonomics (sync/async iterators), parity of consumer-facing APIs, and a minimal surface for implementers to hook platform-specific auth logic.

Motivation and context:
- Customers reported fragility when long-lived streams encountered short-lived credentials or refresh failures; current SDKs either dropped the stream or required heavy client code to resume.
- The goal is to let SDKs automatically swap credentials mid-stream and continue receiving tokens while preserving ordering and backpressure semantics.
- We also want a single, small adapter pattern so language SDKs share the same behavioral contract without forcing identical internals.

What this change does:
- Adds a cursor-adapter abstraction implemented in each SDK: Python (StreamingCursor), TS (CursorAdapter), Go (cursoradapter.Cursor). The adapter exposes a unified contract: peek(), ack(), extendAuth(newToken), and close().
- Implements token-swap reauth which attempts a fast-path auth swap (synchronous in-process) and falls back to a jittered soft-backoff if the provider is unreachable for N attempts.
- Surfaces ergonomics: Python exposes an async generator plus a convenience sync iterator; TS exposes AsyncIterable and a small pull-based helper; Go exposes a channel-backed iterator with context cancellation and explicit Resume() helper.
- Adds tests and e2e harness scenarios simulating short-lived token rotation, intermittent network, and mid-stream model fallback.
- Bumps SDK versions: python 0.18.0, typescript 1.7.0, go v0.9.0.

Checklist (high-level):
- [x] Design doc link: internal doc ID ENG-2147 (attached in Linear)
- [x] Implementation in all three SDKs + unit tests
- [x] Integration tests against the streaming canary harness (perf-canary)
- [x] Docs: quickstart snippet and migration notes in SDK changelogs
- [x] Release notes drafted

Compatibility and migration notes:
- Consumer-facing change is additive; existing streaming code will continue to work. To opt into token-swap behavior consumers must either use the new adapter directly or enable auto-reauth in the client config (off by default).
- There is a small behavioral change for Go: Resume() is now recommended instead of re-creating the iterator for resuming after auth refresh, but old pattern still functions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: mid-stream credential exchange could reorder messages if adapters are misused. Mitigation: adapter enforces single-writer semantics and sequence checks; tests simulate race conditions.
- Risk: aggressive retries could overwhelm auth service. Mitigation: backoff parameters are conservative by default and configurable via client options.

Follow-ups (engineer TODOs):
- Expose metrics: token_swap_attempts, token_swap_success, token_swap_backoff_count (ENG-2203).
- Add an examples repo snippet showing server-initiated rotate flow.
